# Loader layout and remote offload counterexamples

This topic covers loader swaps, stage decomposition and remote CPU/cache offload. Open this topic when a proposed layout change adds representation, coordination, serialization or network costs to an efficient existing path. If the replacement is slower, read both implementations side by side, fix the gaps that explain the slowdown, and verify performance parity before optimizing further.

[Catalog index](../../technique_catalog.md) · [Negative results](../negative_results.md) · {ref}`Compare loader implementations <compare-loader-implementations>`

**`loader_swap_without_data_layout`: a loader swap does not remove payload and transform costs**
- Trigger: A replacement loader runs out of memory while its dataset contains large inline image binaries, or remains slower after moving those payloads to lookup because image-library threading still contends.
- Attempt: Replace the loader without changing a dataset that stores large image binaries inline to meet a storage-request constraint.
- Outcome: The new loader ran out of memory. Moving the payloads out of the dataset and looking up images made loading functional, not faster. Profiling then identified OpenCV's internal TBB threading; disabling it with `cv2.setNumThreads(0)` improved utilization, and the combined loader, dataset and thread-setting changes shortened training. This does not demonstrate a loader-only win.
- Guards and when to revisit: Diagnose representation and transform costs separately from the loader label. First reuse baseline fetch, transform and collate components in a minimal-change comparison. If the layout prevents reuse, explain the blocker and test representation or thread-budget changes separately rather than calling the bundle unchanged-layout parity. Inline payloads may solve a real storage-rate constraint; deferred lookup must still fit that constraint. Preserve row identity, image contents and sampling when changing representation, and count memory and threads across all workers and ranks. Removing inline binaries alone did not fix throughput, and the final bundle does not prove unchanged-layout parity. Even after the thread fix, the process-only path slightly outperformed the threaded/process hybrid in the comparison; equivalent performance across layouts was not established.

**`fused_stage_split_negative`: splitting fused pipeline work can add more overhead than overlap saves**
- Trigger: A pipeline stage already performs several operations together efficiently, but a redesign would schedule them as separate stages. When a small model finishes each training step quickly, extra thread scheduling, context switches, queue handoffs or intermediate copies can cost more than the split saves.
- Attempt: In one measured example, the original worker-local function combined cache lookup, decoding, transforms, padding and collation. It took compact sample indices and returned a complete batch. The split moved collation to the parent, so expanded rows crossed the process boundary.
- Outcome: Serialization, inter-process communication (IPC) and backpressure slowed the cold run, which stopped before completing a full training run. A later split that preserved behavior was slower over the broader comparison window but approached the fused path's speed as the cache warmed. Thread tuning brought late-window performance roughly to parity, not a speedup across the full window. The split was kept for experiments, not because it was faster.
- Guards and when to revisit: Keep the original fused function as the control. Split it only when measurements identify work that can overlap or benefit from independent concurrency. this is not a rule against splitting stages. Measure which cost the split adds rather than assuming context switching caused the slowdown. Preserve worker-local clients, caches, state and random-number streams, as well as batch membership and order; bound intermediate buffers. When crossing processes, prefer passing compact inputs before expansion or finished batches after compaction. Compare complete-path throughput, including the slowest rank, in matched cold and warm windows. The later split passed behavior-parity tests and finished without failures or restarts; the early cold screen does not establish a steady-state penalty. Storage locality and throttling were plausible additional contributors, not isolated causes.

**`local_cache_remote_offload_negative`: remote CPU and cache offload did not beat an efficient local cache**
- Trigger: The baseline loader already reads from a local filesystem cache on each training host, and remote CPU hosts reached by remote procedure calls (RPC) are proposed to add processing or cache capacity.
- Attempt: The remote design retained training ranks and loader workers, used shared remote CPU/cache capacity rather than one cache replica per rank, and routed samples deterministically. A follow-up replaced file-based transport staging with shared-memory staging.
- Outcome: Remote fetch and raw-data caching lost to local loading at every comparable completed epoch in one set of comparisons. Added serialization and network round trips did not pay off over an already-effective local cache. Replacing file-based transport staging with shared-memory staging improved that substage but did not close the training gap. Remaining waits included remote request admission, cache churn and uneven cache budgets.
- Guards and when to revisit: Retain the local path unless a new bottleneck hypothesis shows local CPU or cache capacity limiting the consumer. Test that hypothesis with matched hardware and execution location, comparable cache warmth and mature epochs, counting request, serialization, transfer and reconstruction costs. The comparisons used completed-batch counter deltas and the rank-zero training callback's batch rate, not maximum-rank duration or end-to-end wall time. Hardware, execution locations, packages, cache capacities and warm ages differed, so the observed slowdown was not a controlled causal penalty. Remote runs ended before mature epochs and some stopped early; earlier pilots had no completed-epoch measurements. Missing epochs are not zero-duration results or successful full fits. Host-stage phase measurements overlap and cannot be added as model or GPU-kernel time. These results reject the tested implementation, not remote offload in general. Count remote hosts as added resources, include cold and warm phases and all clients/admission limits, and preserve sample identity, order and error handling.
